text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- The International Monetary Fund has cancelled the standby arrangement worth $850 million and has made future lending conditional on Pakistan bringing about some basic structural reforms in its economy.
- The government is ready to release all Indian fishing boats, trawlers and their crew seized in Pakistani territorial waters provided India reciprocates, a foreign ministry spokesman said.
- The foreign ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Conference will meet on Saturday to finalise the agenda of the special summit scheduled for Sunday.

- The Lahore High Court barred state-run Pakistan Television and Pakistan Radio from relaying cigarette commercials and programmes which might induce people to smoke. The order will take effect from April 1.
- Wasim Sajjad was sworn in as Chairman of the Senate (upper house) for a fourth consecutive term.

- The Japanese government has agreed to provide 720.47 million rupees as a grant for debt relief, implement projects for exploitation of ground water in Punjab province and improving environmental conditions in Quetta.
- A ban imposed on feasts at marriage ceremonies has resulted in a sharp decline in the sale of many food items bringing down their prices in the market.
- The government has decided to give preference to expatriate Pakistanis while selling state-run companies.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said Pakistan has enough foreign exchange reserves and there was no threat of any default in loan payment.
- The IMF has appreciated the supply side strategy of the government, but expressed its concern at a proposed massive tax reduction programme, sources said.
- The Asset Management Trust would start functioning from April for cleansing the bad debt portfolios of state-run banks and financial institutions, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- The government has decided to abide by the contracts awarded to oil and gas exploration companies up to mid-1996, sources said.
FINANCIAL POST
- Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission Hafiz Pasha said the government might announce a steep reduction in import tariffs on raw materials to spur export-oriented industries.
- Pakistan's natural gas reserves will dry up by the year 2010, disclosed Javed Hameed, managing director of state-run Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Ltd.
- Net annual profits of state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd are expected to fall by 6.6 percent from the previous level of 16.835 billion rupees, analysts said.
